narrative:
AstraZeneca Revenue in the Q3 Forecast is USD 63.3B, +0.8% against the USD 62.8B budget.

Oncology is the largest therapy area at USD 30.2B (48% of group). Respiratory & Immunology is furthest ahead of plan (USD 0.3B); Vaccines & Immune Therapies is furthest behind (USD -0.2B).

Key risk: the Vaccines & Immune Therapies gap widens if the volume drivers on the Scenarios page move against plan.

signals.title: Q3 hard close locked at WD+5, two days faster than Q2. US gross-to-net accruals are still the last item to lock
signals.source: SDP Group Close Control Tower — 8 close feeds, September 2026 quarter-end
signals.excerpt: The September quarter-end close locked at WD+5 against WD+7 in Q2. 91.4% of balance-sheet reconciliations were auto-certified, and USD 486M was still unreconciled at WD+3. 61% of that (USD 297M) sits in US gross-to-net accruals, driven by the Medicare Part D redesign and 340B contract-pharmacy claims.

signals.title: Intercompany mismatch of USD 212M at quarter-end: goods in transit to the US and CNY rate timing
signals.source: SDP Intercompany & Consolidation — 7 flow types, USD 34.0B of annual intra-group flows
signals.excerpt: Of USD 8.5B of Q3 intercompany flows, USD 212M was not agreed by WD+2: product supply to the US in transit at 30 September (USD 96M), AstraZeneca China CNY rate timing (USD 58M), Alexion recharge cost-centre mapping (USD 41M) and royalty true-ups (USD 17M). Every break now has an owner and an evidence pack.

signals.title: USD 118M of Q3 clinical trial accruals were still estimate-only at WD+2
signals.source: SDP Close Control — CRO and investigator-site accruals
signals.excerpt: Clinical trial accruals of USD 1.6B for Q3 were 92.6% confirmed by CRO and site data at WD+2. The remaining USD 118M is concentrated in three late-stage oncology programmes with new CRO partners. The accrual agent matches patient-visit data to contract milestones and proposes the true-up for controller approval.
